name: Captain Vigdis Ironhollow
lines: The Corp's own patrol cutter, lent to every traveller who takes off from the Spaceport: sleek, steady and kind to a new pilot. Its phasers stun; the Corp does not kill.
The shuttle you bought at the Transport Yard: a broad-shouldered hull, a roomy cabin and a heavy heat shield. Slower than a fighter, but it takes a beating.
Your flying saucer
The saucer you bought at the Transport Yard. Its rim spins a field round the whole hull, so its shields are strong; it fires a ring of light from under the dome.
The Twinvane Shrike
The one-seat fighter found on the Moon: the quickest ship in the sky, with twin cannons under its chin.
The Corsair Kestrel
The battered light freighter found on Pluto. Its dorsal turret swings to wherever you look, so it hits what it aims at even while it turns.
Ashvaal, the Pearl Domeship
The Veyari domeship found on Veyar. Its shields are the strongest of any ship, and its turrets and lances strike hard and slow, and its battle pods drop from beneath on the second gun.
Nightwyrm, the Black Dragon
The black dragon engine found on Venus. It flies the dark as well as any ship, and its shadow flame burns through shields.
Emberwing, the Red Phoenix
The phoenix engine found on Mercury. Its shoulder cannons throw a spread of sun-fire, three bolts at a time.

The grey raiders came through the Far Gate long ago; some of them crashed in Ironfray's Glass Crater. Past Mars they still prey on traders and travellers.
Ships are knocked out, never destroyed: raider crews eject in pods and the Space Corp picks them up.
Dues-paying dreamers are paid a bounty for each strike they break, a few times a day.

Ilsa, the Rose Sun
An orange-red star, a little smaller and cooler than our Sun
K-type star (orange dwarf), seen rose through the Reach's dust
Teth, the Blue Sun: they circle each other

Most stars in our galaxy are smaller and cooler than our Sun. Orange dwarfs like Ilsa shine steadily for tens of billions of years, so astronomers think their planets are good places to look for life.
Stars that come in pairs are called binary stars. About half the Sun-like stars we know have at least one partner.
Teth, the Blue Sun
A small, hot blue-white star
A small hot star, blue-white
Hotter stars shine bluer: Teth's surface is over 9,000 °C
A star's colour tells its temperature: red stars are the coolest, then orange, yellow, white, and blue is hottest.
On Veyar, the two suns make two shadows of everything, one rose and one blue.
Home world of the Veyari
The Veyari: tall, calm, star-faring
Two, rose and blue
Ilvessa, the Singing City
The Veyari built the watch-station by Neptune and came through the Far Gate long ago, curious about the blue world.
Planets that circle a pair of stars are called circumbinary planets. The first one confirmed, Kepler-16b, was found in 2011.
An ocean world: no land at all, only sea and reefs
The Ondai, gentle giant reef-builders who sing
Ocean everywhere, with floating reef-towns
Astronomers think some planets may be 'ocean worlds', covered in water hundreds of kilometres deep.
In our own Solar System, Jupiter's moon Europa and Saturn's moon Enceladus hide oceans of liquid water under their ice.
A green-gold gas giant with rings
Gas giant, mostly hydrogen and helium
Ice and dust, lit gold by Ilsa
Tullimar, the Tullik market moon
Every giant planet in our Solar System has rings: Saturn's are the brightest, but Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune have them too.
A ring is made of countless bits of ice and rock, each on its own orbit.
The Tullik market moon
The Tullik, small big-headed traders
A market that never closes, spice cake that fizzes, rocks that hum
Hoon, the gas giant
Moons can be worlds in their own right: Saturn's moon Titan is bigger than the planet Mercury and has a thick air.
Pip-Tullik, the trader you meet out past Saturn, was born here.
The machine world of the Orrem, gone silent
The Orrem: thinking machines, makers of the survey drones
Silent for a very long time
Plated over, with towers and long lines of light
The Orrem sent their survey drones out to map every world. Then they stopped answering. Nobody knows why.
Real space probes have flown out of our Solar System: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is more than 24 billion km away and still sending a faint signal home.
A world of red stone and great fortresses
The Hrovan: stone-skinned, proud, honourable duellists
Red rock, deep canyons and fortress-cities
Strong: a third more than Earth's
The Hrovan respect only those who have beaten their champion in a fair fight. Win, and they will fly beside you.
A planet bigger than Earth but made of rock is called a super-Earth. Many have been found around other stars.
Cinder and the Ashen Drift
A dead moon in a field of wrecks: the grey raiders' hold
Wrecks of a thousand ships, and the raiders' fortress hulk
The raiders' patrols fly here day and night
The grey raiders strip every ship they catch and add it to the Drift. Some of their ships still wear Space Corp paint.
Stay clear unless you come to fight.
A nebula: a cloud of glowing gas
A nebula is a cloud of gas and dust in space. New stars are born where the cloud is thickest.
The pink glow comes from hydrogen gas lit by young stars; the blue-green from oxygen. The Orion Nebula, visible to the naked eye from Earth, glows the same way.
An ancient Veyari beacon
The Veyari say the Lantern was lit to guide their first ships home through the Far Gate, and has never once gone out.
Lighthouses for ships in space are real ideas: pulsars, dead stars that spin, give off beams so regular they could be used to find your way across the galaxy.
A derelict Orrem ark
A huge machine ship, dark and drifting
The ark's last log, still running on a weak power cell: "All minds aboard. Destination: the world beyond the Gate. Reason: the grey ones came." So the Orrem fled the raiders.
A ship meant to carry people for generations between the stars is called a generation ship. None has been built, but scientists have worked out what one would need.
Kethrin, a brown dwarf
A failed star, glowing deep red
A brown dwarf is bigger than Jupiter but too small for its core to burn hydrogen like a star. It glows dull red from the heat left over from when it formed.
The first brown dwarfs were confirmed in 1995. Some are so cool you could, in theory, stand near one without burning.
A comet that belongs to no sun
Comets are lumps of ice and dust. Some are thrown out of their home system and wander between the stars.
In 2017 astronomers saw ‘Oumuamua, the first object known to come into our Solar System from another star. A second, comet Borisov, followed in 2019.
A gutted ship with a Space Corp number on its hull
The hull carries an old Space Corp number under the raiders' red paint. The raiders did not build this ship; they took it.
Its chart is still in the console: every line on it leads to Cinder and the Ashen Drift.
The Far Reach. Two suns ahead, rose and blue, and Veyar turning between them. Other worlds are out here, and other peoples. M opens the chart of the Reach; the gate behind you takes you home.
Home sky. The Far Gate is behind you, Pluto ahead, and the Sun a bright star a long way in.

Tullimar, the market moon
Hoon fills half the sky, green and gold, its rings a bridge of light. Down here the Tullik market never closes.
Maru-Ondo, the ocean world
No land at all: only the sea, and the great floating reefs the Ondai grow and sing into shape.
Orr, the silent machine world
Plates of metal to the horizon, towers with their lights still burning, and no voice anywhere. The Orrem are here, but they do not answer.
Skeldmar, the red stone world
Red rock and deep canyons under a heavy pull: every step is work. On the ridge stand the fortress-halls of the Hrovan.
A shard of the Singing Crystal
Light on your path
Find the Sael Lantern, out in the Reach, and scan it. Bring its reading to Ilun on Veyar.
A humming rock that hums your name
The barge to Veyar
A Tullik barge of spice cake is going to Veyar, and the raiders know it. Fly with it from Tullimar to Veyar and keep it safe.
A pearl from the deep reef
The song of the Veil
The Ondai sing the shapes of their reefs from songs of the sky. Scan the Veil of Sael, the great nebula, and bring its song to Elder Moana-Rhu.
An Orrem memory-core, still warm
Why the Orrem went quiet
Find the derelict Orrem ark adrift in the Reach and read its last log. Bring it to the Archive on Orr.
A Hrovan honour-blade (a keepsake, never sharpened)
Meet Kaldra the Unbowed, champion of the Hrovan, ship to ship above Skeldmar. Knock her ship out fairly and the Hrovan will fly beside you.
Their ships will fly beside you in the Reach's battles.
They give you a gift:
The peoples you know
Mother of the Market
A visitor from the blue world! Sit, sit. Cake? It fizzes. You fly? Good. I have work for a pilot, and the pay is friendship, which is worth more than gold. Most days.
Eldest Singer of the Reef
Little traveller from the dry world, welcome to the reef. Listen: the water is singing. Will you sit with me while it does?
The Archive of Orr
The last mind still awake
Tower-tender, still at work
Garden keeper of a garden of metal
Kaldra the Unbowed
Champion of the Hrovan
A small soft one from the blue world, standing in my hall. Brave or foolish? Meet me ship to ship above Skeldmar and we will find out.

A friendly swap: they remember who trades fairly
A fair swap. The Tullik like you a little better for it.
The stalls have had all your trade they can take today. Come back tomorrow.

You have not found it yet.
Ilun holds the reading to the light and smiles. "So the Lantern still burns. Then our first ships were not lost. Thank you, friend."
Elder Moana-Rhu closes her eyes and hums the Veil's song back to you. Out on the reef, the coral begins to grow in a new shape.
The Archive is silent a long time. "They fled the grey ones. They meant to come back for me." Its eye glows a little brighter. "Thank you for telling me. I am not forgotten."

The barge is waiting for you above Tullimar.
the barge Spice Wind
The barge to Veyar. Take off: the barge Spice Wind waits above Tullimar. Fly up beside it and press E when you are ready.
Spice Wind , Ollo-Tullik at the helm: "Off we go! Stay close, pilot, I can smell raiders." The barge turns for Veyar.
Raiders on the barge! Ollo-Tullik: "They are after the cake! Help!"
The Spice Wind is crippled. Ollo-Tullik limps home in the life-pod, unhurt. "Next time, pilot!" You can try again from the Matron's stall.
The barge to Veyar: done. The Spice Wind settles toward Veyar with every cake whole. Ollo-Tullik: "You fly like a Tullik! Matron will hear of this."
Kaldra laughs. "You beat me once. Once is enough for the sagas."
Kaldra's longship, the Unbowed
The champion's challenge. Take off: Kaldra's longship will meet you above Skeldmar. No allies, no Corp, ship to ship. Knock her out and the Hrovan will fly beside you.
Kaldra: "There you are, small one. Shields up. Fight well!" Her longship swings in, banner flying.
Kaldra: "Ha! Knocked out fair and square. Skeldmar will sing of you. When you fight in the Reach, the Hrovan fly beside you."
Kaldra's voice on the comm: "Good fight. Mend your ship and come again."
